title: Alfred the Great
objective: After this level you can explain how Alfred defended Wessex against the Vikings.
summary: Alfred of Wessex (871-899) survived the Viking attack of 878, won at Edington, agreed a Danelaw border and defended Wessex with burhs, ships and learning.

cards.headline: In 878 a king of Wessex was hiding in a marsh. He became “Alfred the Great”.
cards.body: He is the only English monarch known as “the Great”. He had lost almost everything to a Viking army. Here’s how he won it back.

cards.headline: Down to the marshes
cards.body: A great Danish army arrived in England in 865. Alfred became king of Wessex, one of Level 9’s Anglo-Saxon kingdoms, in 871. In early 878 the Danes seized Chippenham, and the West Saxons submitted, all except Alfred. He withdrew to the Somerset marshes and fought on. The famous tale of him letting a peasant woman’s cakes burn there? A legend, first written down long after his death.

cards.headline: Edington, then a border
cards.body: In May 878 Alfred beat the Danes at Edington. Their leader, Guthrum, was baptized a Christian with Alfred as his godfather. In 886 Alfred and the Danes agreed a frontier along the old Roman road, Watling Street. The Danish-ruled north and east became known as the Danelaw, “Danes’ law”. The Vikings were no longer just raiders. They were neighbours.

cards.headline: Never more than 20 miles
cards.body: Then Alfred built. He covered Wessex with fortified towns called burhs, placed so that no part of the kingdom was more than 20 miles from one. He had a navy of fast new ships built. And he had Latin books translated into English, taking part in the work himself. Wessex was never again in such danger.

mascot.line: Walls, ships and books. Alfred defended Wessex with all three.
